questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Generic Engineering & Type Transformation Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What does the expression 'K extends keyof T' signify in a TypeScript generic function signature?

options.text: That K is a numeric index array.
That K must be a valid property name (key) belonging to type T.
That K inherits all methods from class T.
That K converts type T into a string.

questions.explanation: 'keyof T' generates the union of keys of T; 'K extends keyof T' constrains K to strictly those valid key names.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Generic Engineering & Type Transformation Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why is 'function wrap<T>(item: T): T' superior to 'function wrap(item: any): any'?

options.text: Generics compile directly into C++ structs.
Generics preserve the specific input type, retaining autocomplete and type validation for the caller.
Generics make the function run asynchronously.
Generics encrypt the input parameter in memory.

questions.explanation: 'any' silences the compiler and discards type tracking, whereas generics capture and propagate the exact type forward.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Generic Engineering & Type Transformation Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What does the '-?' modifier do in a TypeScript mapped type?

options.text: It removes optionality, making all properties strictly required.
It removes null values from union types.
It reverses the order of properties.

questions.explanation: The '-?' modifier removes optionality from each property, converting optional fields (x?) into mandatory fields.

questions.prompt: Which utility type should you choose to create an object type mapping a fixed set of HTTP status codes to string descriptions?
questions.explanation: Record<K, T> creates an object type whose property keys are K and property values are T.
